resources.string: Connected to the hub via SSH tunnel
Connected to the hub through the local proxy
Not in use: direct connection to the hub works
Not in use: connected to the hub through the SSH tunnel
Not in use: connected to the hub through the local proxy
If this device can\'t reach the hub\'s address (different network, no VPN), you can go through an SSH server that can reach the hub.

Add the “authorized_keys line” to this user\'s ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the SSH server. It carries restrict and permitopen, so this key can only forward to the tunnel target below and can\'t open a shell. The private key is kept encrypted on this device only.
Can\'t read this device\'s SSH key right now (unlock the device and try again)
An SSH server this device can reach and that can reach the hub. For bastion hosts like Warpgate, write the username as user:target.
The hub\'s address as seen from the SSH server. If the hub runs on that server, use 127.0.0.1:18660.
Verified on first connection. If the server\'s fingerprint changes later, the connection is refused, never accepted automatically.

When off, the app connects to the hub directly first and only uses the SSH tunnel if that fails, then checks every 2 minutes whether the direct connection works again. The tunnel retries automatically after it disconnects.
Signs in to the SSH server with the settings above and opens one forward to the tunnel target.
Persona stops using this SSH server to reach the hub. You\'ll need to remove the authorized_keys line on the server yourself.
%1$s %2$s\n\nOn the server, run ssh-keygen -lf on its host public key and trust it only if the fingerprints match. If the fingerprint changes later, the connection is refused.

Pinned: %1$s
Now: %2$s

The server may have been reinstalled or changed its key, or someone may be in the middle. Trust it only after confirming the server changed its key.
Can\'t reach %1$s:%2$s (%3$s). Check the address and port, and whether this device can reach it.
The server\'s fingerprint needs confirming first
The server\'s fingerprint changed, so the connection was refused

The SSH server didn\'t accept this device\'s public key. Add the line from Copy authorized_keys line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for %1$s on the server (Warpgate: add it to this user\'s public keys), then try again.
SSH handshake failed (%1$s). Check that the server supports Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA-SHA2 host keys.
Signed in, but the server couldn\'t open a forward to %1$s (%2$s). Check the tunnel target, that the hub is on that port, and that the permitopen address in authorized_keys matches this one.
The tunnel was closed while it was starting. Try again.

A SOCKS5 proxy that another app on this device provides, such as a VPN-like client that serves 127.0.0.1 instead of taking the system VPN slot. Persona\'s traffic to the hub, this device\'s credential included, goes through it unencrypted, even for an https hub: you\'re trusting whatever app holds that port.
This proxy isn\'t on this device: Persona\'s traffic to the hub, this device\'s credential and the proxy\'s password would cross the network unencrypted.
Only if the proxy asks for one. It\'s kept encrypted on this device with this hub\'s pairing.
The hub\'s HTTP address as seen from the proxy. Leave it empty to use the paired address.

When off, the app connects to the hub directly first and only uses the proxy if that fails, then checks every 2 minutes whether the direct connection works again. Only Persona\'s traffic to the hub goes through the proxy.
Connects through the proxy to the hub\'s address and checks that the hub answers.
Persona stops using this proxy to reach the hub.
Can\'t reach the proxy at %1$s (%2$s). Check that the app providing it is running, and its port.
%1$s didn\'t answer as a SOCKS5 proxy. Check the port; HTTP proxies aren\'t supported.
The proxy couldn\'t connect to %1$s (%2$s). Check the hub\'s address as seen from the proxy.
The proxy asks for a username and password
The proxy accepts neither no login nor a username and password
The proxy didn\'t accept the username or password
The proxy\'s answer doesn\'t follow SOCKS5
The proxy didn\'t answer in time
The username and password can each be at most 255 bytes
The hub\'s address must be 1 to 255 bytes long
Got no answer from %1$s through the proxy: the proxy may not reach that address, or the hub isn\'t listening there.
Reached %1$s through the proxy, but it doesn\'t look like a hub (/api/v1/health didn\'t answer properly). Check the hub\'s address and port.
%1$s is another hub, not the one this device is paired with. Check the hub\'s address.
The hub at %1$s treats connections through the proxy as coming from the internet and refuses plain HTTP from there. Enter the hub\'s address inside its LAN or VPN.
